newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Striking Venezuelan doctors blamed for six deaths.
newsitem.headline: Striking Venezuelan doctors blamed for six deaths.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has blamed striking doctors for six deaths since they walked out of hospitals last Friday, leaving emergency wards unattended.
Public Minister Ivan Dario Badell said there would be an investigation, the leading daily El Universal reported on Tuesday.
But union representatives of Venezuela's 27,000 public doctors, who have asked for a 1,000-percent pay rise, said the government was to blame.
"It well knew what would happen and should have been prepared for this," Venezuelan Medics Federation (FMV) president Fernando Blanco told El Universal.
Venezuelan doctors earn an average $126 per month in a public health system notoriously underfunded and poorly supplied.
Over the weekend unattended mothers gave birth in hospital doorways and patients went untreated as overstretched military doctors staffed emergency wards throughout the country.
Medics have so far ignored a presidential decree that ordered them back to work on Friday, a seven-day truce and a 25 percent pay offer.
"They have taken the Venezuelan poor hostage and are simply decreeing death sentences to those that arrive at emergency wards in a serious condition," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
"The expectation of a $1,000 minimum salary, however just it might be, is just outside the reach of the Venezuelan economy," he added.
A further 2,500 army medics will man Caracas hospitals as of Tuesday, El Universal reported.
